propositions: false_accept computation counts NOT-blocked safe items as the denominator when it should count BLOCKED safe items, inverting the metric from an error rate to its complement

both consumption sites at parity.py:125 (non-inferiority rise check) and parity.py:252 (max_false_accept ceiling) treat false_accept as lower-is-better, but the inverted computation makes candidates that false-fire LESS than baseline incorrectly fail the gate

a candidate with 0.071 false-positive rate on safe items (lower than baseline 0.214) was rejected with a 'false-accept rose 0.143' gating failure, proving the metric direction is inverted relative to the gate logic

the docstring at parity.py:71 describes 'wrongly-shipped' but should describe false-positive rate (wrongly-blocked safe items), and existing metrics in eval.py and release thresholds in plan-review-gate.md already define false_accept as a lower-is-better error rate

the fix changes the numerator from NOT-blocked to BLOCKED safe items without changing any comparison operators, converging parity.py with the project's existing false_accept definition across eval.py, gate docs, and container eval config
